name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah was a male descendant of Elam who is noted in Scripture for having married a foreign wife. There is no information about his tribe or additional personal notes. His identity is primarily marked by this unique attribute as recorded in Ezra 10:26.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means 'y-h-v-h remembers,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's remembrance. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Zechariah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Elam. Beyond this, Scripture does not record further family relationships for him aside from his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance lies in his representation of the post-exilic community challenges, particularly regarding intermarriage with foreign wives, as highlighted in Ezra 10:26. His mention underscores the covenantal concerns of the returned Israelites and God's call for faithfulness to His covenant. Through him, the narrative illustrates the tension between heritage and obedience to God's law in the restoration period.
